plugins.readme:
# Students Pro

Advanced: hooks, events, services, guards, layout, extension points, dependency on Stats.

## What you get

- **Hooks** on the host operation `item.create`: trims names and vetoes empty ones
- A **route guard** and a **plugin layout**
- A **PRO badge** in the title bar and a dashboard toolbar action
- A dependency on *Stats Service* (activated first)

## How to use it

1. Open **Plugins** and make sure *Students Pro* is enabled.
2. Look for its entries in the sidebar, the menu bar and the dashboard.
3. Open the plugin's page in **Plugins → Details** to change its settings and read its logs.

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `hooks` | intercepting host operations |
| `events` | reacting to `item.created` |
| `services` | reading the stats service |

## Good to know

> Plugins are shipped as built JavaScript only. Source code never leaves the author's machine.

Documentation: [fluxplugin on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/fluxplugin)

plugins.name: Appearance
plugins.description: Themes, accent colors, fonts, text size, density and more — everything about how the app looks.
plugins.author: fluxplugin
plugins.readme:
# Appearance

Make the app yours. This plugin adds an **Appearance** page to *Settings* and four extra themes.

## What you can change

- **Mode** — System, Light or Dark.
- **Theme** — Midnight, Sunset, Forest or high-contrast Graphite.
- **Accent color** — seven colors, or the theme's own.
- **Text** — font family, any font installed on your computer, size and line spacing.
- **Layout** — compact or comfortable spacing, corner roundness, translucency and reduced motion.

> [!TIP]
> Type the name of any font installed on your computer in *Your own font*. If it is missing, the next font in the list is used.

## How it works

| Setting | Stored as |
| --- | --- |
| Theme and mode | the app's theme variables |
| Fonts, size, spacing | CSS variables on the page |

Your choices are saved on this device and apply to every plugin, because plugins use the same variables.

## For developers

Plugins can add their own **themes** and **fonts** to the same lists — see the `theme` and `font` extension points in the documentation.

plugins.author: fluxplugin examples
plugins.readme:
# Stats Service

Main + renderer plugin: validated IPC, preload API, pushed events and a typed config.

## What you get

- A **main-process** service answering validated IPC calls (`stats.get`, `stats.addStudent`)
- A **preload API** exposed as `window.plugins.stats`
- A live **push** (`stats.updated`) every few seconds, with a configurable interval
- A typed, persisted **configuration** (see *Settings*)

## How to use it

1. Open **Plugins** and make sure *Stats Service* is enabled.
2. Look for its entries in the sidebar, the menu bar and the dashboard.
3. Open the plugin's page in **Plugins → Details** to change its settings and read its logs.

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `ipc` | handlers and push events |
| `services` | the `stats.service` other plugins can use |
| `storage` | persisting its settings |

## Good to know

> Plugins are shipped as built JavaScript only. Source code never leaves the author's machine.

Documentation: [fluxplugin on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/fluxplugin)

# Calendar Pro

One or two sentences that say what this plugin does and who it is for.

## What you get

- A **page** at `/calendar_pro` in the sidebar
- A **widget** on the dashboard
- A **command** you can run from the command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K)

## How to use it

1. Enable the plugin in **Plugins**.
2. Open **Calendar Pro** in the sidebar.
3. Configure it in the plugin's *Settings* section.

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `routes`, `menus` | adds its page and sidebar entry |
| `ui` | adds a dashboard widget |
| `commands` | registers its commands |

## Video & screenshots

Add them in `plugin.json` and they appear on this page:

```json
"video": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YOUR_VIDEO_ID",
"banner": "./assets/banner.png",
"screenshots": ["./assets/shot-1.png", "./assets/shot-2.png"],
"links": { "docs": "https://example.com/docs", "support": "https://example.com/support" }
```

## Changelog

- **1.0.0** — first release

# Dashboard Widgets

Renderer-only plugin: a lazy route, a dashboard widget, a toolbar action and scoped styles.

## What you get

- A **widget** on the dashboard (slot `dashboard.after`)
- A lazy-loaded **Analytics** page with a sidebar entry
- A **toolbar action** contributed to the host's `dashboard` extension point
- A command with the shortcut `Mod+Shift+R`

## How to use it

1. Open **Plugins** and make sure *Dashboard Widgets* is enabled.
2. Look for its entries in the sidebar, the menu bar and the dashboard.
3. Open the plugin's page in **Plugins → Details** to change its settings and read its logs.

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `routes, menus` | its page and sidebar entry |
| `ui` | widget + toolbar contribution |
| `commands` | the refresh command |
| `styles` | its own CSS, removed when disabled |

## Good to know

> Plugins are shipped as built JavaScript only. Source code never leaves the author's machine.

Documentation: [fluxplugin on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/fluxplugin)

plugins.name: Language
plugins.description: Use the app in English, French, Spanish or German — and add your own language.
plugins.author: fluxplugin
plugins.readme:
# Language

Choose the language of the whole interface: menus, search, notifications, settings and the plugin manager.

## Languages included

| Language | Code |
| --- | --- |
| English | `en` |
| Français | `fr` |
| Español | `es` |
| Deutsch | `de` |

Open **Settings → Language** and pick one. The change is instant and remembered.

## Add your own language

1. Copy `src/messages.ts` and translate the values.
2. Add the language to the list in `src/renderer.tsx`.
3. Build with `fluxplugin build`.

> [!NOTE]
> Any plugin can ship translations — the app merges them. Missing words fall back to English, so a partial translation is fine.

## Right-to-left languages

Set `rtl: true` on a language (Arabic, Hebrew…) and the whole interface mirrors automatically.
